note: The three lands, read through lore.land's ?/ door (lore.land/?/boon.land, …/*a-room; book/scripts/modules/lands.mjs, painted by /texture/). Canon and guards: .spw/surfaces/three-lands.spw. Every room has one plain rule, stated and never explained; residents are said by what they do and what they want; nobody speaks. A room twinned with a chapter is the room that chapter leans toward, and that chapter carries a door back (its relatedRoutes, kicker Twinned). Portable for the lands' own hosts: no markup, no lore.land paths in the words.

lands.question: What could this become?
lands.danger: Everything can happen, so nothing has to happen yet.
lands.welcome: Welcome to boon.land. Population: to be decided.
lands.weather: the morning before something, all day
bylaws: No plan may be finished before somebody has enjoyed it.
Every maybe is kept on file, and the file is watered.
Doors are to be left open, undecided and dusted.
lands.berries: boon.land grows boonberries and does not pick them. Better in every bowl, and the bowls are all promised.

rooms.rule: Every door is open and none of them has been decided.
rooms.residents: hosts who hold invitations to things nobody has planned yet, and are delighted every time one is accepted

rooms.rule: Pick one boonberry and the tree offers you three more, which is why nobody picks.
rooms.residents: pickers who stand under the branches all season, deciding

rooms.rule: Everything happens here once before it happens anywhere.
rooms.residents: an audience that applauds every rehearsal and leaves before the performance

rooms.rule: A lantern is lent to anyone walking somewhere they have not decided on, and comes back lit.
rooms.residents: lamplighters who lend more light than they own, and keep no count of it
rooms.want: for the walk to have been worth the oil

rooms.rule: A Thursday is planned here, carefully and in advance, for whenever one goes missing.
rooms.residents: planners who have kept one spare Thursday ready every week for years and have never once had to use it

rooms.rule: Anything that falls from a height lands in flour, and the flour is pleased to see it.
rooms.residents: millers who stand under tall things on windy days, just in case

rooms.rule: A pie is promised to everyone; it has not been baked.
rooms.residents: a queue that is very patient and somewhat hungry

rooms.rule: The table is laid for everyone who might come, and a chair is added every time somebody almost does.
rooms.residents: hosts who count chairs instead of guests
rooms.want: for the room to run out of wall before it runs out of chairs

rooms.rule: One furrow is kept open, always, for whatever arrives without a receipt.
rooms.residents: nobody lives in it; everyone steps round it the way you step round a sleeping dog

lands.question: What will this cost?
lands.danger: Mistaking a measurable outcome for a meaningful one.
lands.welcome: Welcome to bane.land. This sign has been charged to your account.
bylaws: Every free sample will be followed, in due course, by its invoice.
Complaints are welcome, and are counted as usage.
Queueing is free. Leaving the queue is a service.
lands.berries: bane.land keeps baneberries in bowls on desks. Never a snack: a pinch sets a jam, keeps a pickle, cuts a sweetness that has gone too far, wakes a sauce, dyes cloth the colour of a storm. Who keeps the bowl full is never said.

rooms.rule: Every wish is stamped on arrival, and its price arrives later, in another register.
rooms.residents: a queue waiting to be told what they have already paid
rooms.want: the stamp to be a nice colour

rooms.rule: Things too small to want are sold to the highest bidder, who never wanted them.
rooms.residents: bidders who win everything and keep it in a drawer

rooms.rule: The floor is still paying for a wish made before the floor was laid, and you can hear every instalment.
rooms.residents: clerks in felt slippers who step over the loud boards
rooms.want: the last payment, which nobody has seen

rooms.rule: An empire one hallway wide, with a crown, a ledger and a gate; the only citizen is also the gate.
rooms.residents: the citizen, who lets himself through on weekdays

rooms.rule: Everything that arrives is recorded three times, correctly, and no two records agree.
rooms.residents: recorders who are each right and have stopped mentioning it
rooms.want: a fourth record, to settle it

rooms.rule: Every seat is assigned by importance, and the order is reissued whenever somebody sits down.
rooms.residents: ushers carrying brass place markers in both hands

rooms.rule: Every question is answered yes or no, including the ones shaped like a square.
rooms.residents: clerks who fold the square ones in half and file both halves

rooms.rule: Every window has a price on it, and the price goes up while the glass is whole.
rooms.residents: glaziers, who are the only people in the land who look out of windows

rooms.rule: Four judges each sentence you through a different window, and all four sentences are served at once.
rooms.residents: judges who have never met, and agree about that

rooms.rule: A bowl of baneberries sits on the desk of whoever is in charge; nobody eats from it, and it is full again every morning.
rooms.residents: whoever is in charge this week

rooms.rule: One Thursday a week is billed here to whoever cannot remember it.
rooms.residents: account holders who are fairly sure they were somewhere

lands.question: What will remain?
bylaws: Nothing is thrown away until someone has asked what it was holding up.
A thing may be called old only after it has been checked.
Lunch is at the bench. The bench is also checked.
lands.berries: bone.land eats boneberries at the bench. Grown, not raised.

rooms.rule: Roads are kept the way they were walked, not the way they were drawn.
rooms.residents: surveyors who follow the ruts with a measuring wheel and apologise to the maps
rooms.want: a map that agrees with the feet

rooms.rule: A promise made here is pressed into stone, and the stone is checked each spring for wear.
rooms.residents: masons who read the grooves with a thumb

rooms.rule: Old defaults are kept in layers, like rock, for those who still stand on them.
rooms.residents: readers who come back after years and find their floor still there
rooms.want: to find their floor still there

rooms.rule: Every mended thing carries the maker's mark and a tooth mark.
rooms.residents: menders who argue gently about which mark came first

rooms.rule: Everything shows how it is held up; a beam that does not answer when tapped is asked again tomorrow.
rooms.residents: joiners who tap, listen and write down what the timber said

rooms.rule: The bridge is one long bone; the dogs would like it, and the keepers would like everyone across it first.
rooms.residents: keepers, a dog, and whoever is halfway over
rooms.want: everyone carried safely, and the chewable end

rooms.rule: Everything is measured from fourteen inches up, the height that knows.
rooms.residents: dogs, mostly, and anyone who has dropped something

rooms.rule: Joiners eat boneberries at the bench and say grown, not raised, and say nothing else about it.
rooms.residents: joiners, at lunch

crossings.boon.land: a window that has not chosen its view
crossings.bane.land: a window with a price on it
crossings.bone.land: a pane kept because it was tested

crossings.boon.land: the one you have not picked yet

crossings.bane.land: a gate that is also the citizen
crossings.bone.land: a crossing that has to stay open
a layer in the library with nothing pressed into it
